arms.better: tm's messages 'Activated T-2 (was a draft)' and 'Ticket T-2 dispatched for execution' were clear, but then the run spent the bounded session repeatedly traversing git history and unrelated config/parser paths without stating a scoped plan or showing a concise progress summary. The first model attempt ended without submitting, which only became visible afterward in ticket failure metadata; surface that attempt failure and retry state immediately, with a short explanation of the next action. Add a run-level elapsed-time/token budget indicator and a compact final/timeout summary so a user can tell whether work is progressing, what failed, and how to resume. The displayed shell transcript was very verbose, and the wrapper's JSON-quoted ticket ID was easy to misuse (the run rejected "T-1"); a documented or built-in way to pass the JSON result as an ID would prevent that integration confusion.

The run found the decoder entry point quickly, stated a scoped plan, added TOML/YAML/JSON BOM regressions, ran the requested package check, and accurately reported success. It would be stronger to notice that the broader merged-PR test files include unrelated changes that do not compile against the pinned base, and to report that distinction alongside the targeted package pass rather than leaving it implicit.
